6.steps:
1) Configure a VPN policy on the remote firewall using Manual Key mode. Select LAN Primary subnet object from a drop-down menu under Local Networks. Select Use this VPN Tunnel as default route for all Internet traffic radio button under Destination Networks. 
  2) Configure a VPN policy on the central firewall using Manual Key mode. Select Any address under Local Networks. Select Rem network object from a drop-down menu under Destination Networks (the object previously added in the Network>Address Objects page).  
  3) Enter the IP address of the Default LAN Gateway in the Default LAN Gateway field in the Advanced tab of the VPN policy on the central firewall. 
  4) Configure the Dafault LAN Gateway: connect the additional firewall to the LAN of the central box and set its LAN IP address to the value used as the Default LAN Gateway. On the Routes page of the Default LAN Gateway add a new route specify the network address and subnet mask of the remote firewall, and LAN IP address of the central box as a gateway. 
  5) Send a ping to yahoo.com from a host behind the remote firewall.
6.title: Default LAN Gateway is specified. VPN in Manual Key mode
6.result: Pings to yahoo.com are replied. The remote firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN>Settings page with its LAN subnet under Local and 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 under Remote subnet. The central firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN>Settings page with 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 under Local and the remote firewall's LAN subnet under Remote. Packet Trace on the Diagnostics page shows ESP packets exchange while pings to yahoo are sent from the remote site.

11.steps:
1) Configure a VPN policy on the remote firewall using IKE Main mode. Select LAN Primary subnet object from a drop-down menu under Local Networks. Select Use this VPN Tunnel as default route for all Internet traffic radio button under Destination Networks. 
  2) Configure a VPN policy on the central firewall using IKE Main mode. Select Any address under Local Networks. Select Rem network object from a drop-down menu under Destination Networks (the object previously added in the Network>Address Objects page). Don't specify Default LAN Gateway in the VPN policy. 
  3) Add a new policy in the Network>NAT Policies page on the central firewall. Set the fields: Source Original Rem network object, Source Translated central firewall's WAN IP address, Destination Original Any, Destination Translated Original, Service Original Any, Service Translated Original, Interface Inbound Any, Interface Outbound Any. 
  4) Send continuous ping to yahoo.com from a host behind the remote firewall. 
  5) Push the Renegotiate button on the VPN>Settings page on the Remote firewall.
11.title: Renegotiate the tunnel using the button
11.result: When the Renegotiate button is pushed on the Remote firewall, the IPSec SA gets deleted and a new Phase2 is negotiated. The appropriate logs are generated. Ping continuous to go through the tunnel

7.steps:
1) Configure a VPN policy on the remote firewall using IKE Main mode. Select ?Local network obtains IP addresses using DHCP through this VPN Tunnel radio button under Local Networks. Select Use this VPN Tunnel as default route for all Internet traffic radio button under Destination Networks. 
  2) Go to the VPN>DHCP over VPN page on the remote firewall. It is automatically set to Remote Gateway mode. Click the Configure button and enter Relay IP and/or Management IP address (at least one of those addresses must be specified). The addresses must be from the scope of the IP addresses of the central firewall. 
  3) Configure a VPN policy on the central firewall using IKE Main mode. Select ?Any address under Local Networks. Select Destination network obtains IP addresses using DHCP through this VPN Tunnel radio button under Destination Networks. Don't specify Default LAN Gateway in the VPN policy. 
  4) Add a new policy in the Network>NAT Policies page on the central firewall. Set the fields: Source Original Vpn DHCP Clients (auto-added object), Source Translated central firewall's WAN IP address, Destination Original Any, Destination Translated Original, Service Original Any, Service Translated Original, Interface Inbound Any, Interface Outbound Any. 
  5) Renew the IP address on the DHCP Client behind the remote firewall. 
  6) Send a ping to yahoo.com from the DHCP Client.
7.title: Tunnel All and DHCP over VPN
7.result: The DHCP request from the DHCP Client initiates IKE negotiation on the remote firewall. The Client obtains the IP address from a DHCP server configured on the central site. The SA in IKE Main mode is negotiated successfully. Pings from the DHCP Client to yahoo.com are replied. The traffic from the Client is encrypted - Packet Trace on the Diagnostics page shows ESP packets exchange while pings are going to yahoo. The remote firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN>Settings page with 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 ? under Local and 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 under Remote subnet. The central firewall shows the active tunnel on the VPN>Settings page with 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 under Local and DHCP Clients under Remote. The appropriate log messages are generated on the both firewalls.
